kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source's wiring diagram, margin note, mnemonic, and drug table.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the wiring diagram, the two margin arrows, the printed mnemonic, and the four drug rows; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The two-anchor reading of any bladder stem (ANCHOR 1 — NAME THE STATE: the book's own margin arrows are the split — '⊕ sympathetic → ↑ urinary retention.' (STORAGE: fill and hold) vs '⊕ parasympathetic → ↑ urine voiding.' (VOIDING: squeeze and release); ANCHOR 2 — LOCATE THE RECEPTOR, THEN READ THE DRUG ROW: detrusor M₃ = the parasympathetic pump key (contract), detrusor β₃ = the sympathetic capacity key (relax), internal sphincter α₁ = the sympathetic outlet key, external sphincter nicotinic = the somatic voluntary key). The book PRINTS the wiring and the two arrows but never names the two states nor assigns per-structure effect directions to them — the STORAGE-STATE vs VOIDING-STATE framing, the per-structure direction assignments (except where a drug row prints them: M₃ contraction, M₃/β₃ relaxation, α₁-antagonist relaxation), and the reading order (state → receptor → drug row) are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the wiring diagram, the two margin arrows, and the four drug rows as separate elements; the two-state protocol that unifies them is KYP's design (every receptor, arrow, drug name, and application is the book's own).
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms + the visual's state panels

kypExtensions.summary: The anatomical and clinical anchors that extend past the page: the sacral cord levels S2–S4 of the pelvic and pudendal nerves and the Onuf nucleus (the external sphincter's motor home — classic neuroanatomy, NOT printed on the page); the α₁-CONTRACTION direction of the internal urethral sphincter (read off the book's own α1-antagonist row — tamsulosin RELAXES 'smooth muscle (eg, bladder, neck, prostate)', so α₁ stimulation contracts the outlet — a KYP reading, not a printed sentence); the nicotinic/pudendal VOLUNTARY-HOLD reading of the external sphincter (the page prints only the 'Pudendal nerve (somatic input)' + 'Nicotinic receptor' labels); the outlet-obstruction-vs-detrusor-failure sorting of urinary retention (the BPH row implies it — obstruction at the outlet answers to α₁ blockade, not to a stronger pump; the sorting frame is KYP); and the stress-vs-urgency incontinence sorting (the table's 'Urgency incontinence' application implies the detrusor-overactivity mechanism; the stress-incontinence contrast is KYP). The structure × receptor × nerve × drug × application KEY MAP (the note's second table) is KYP's pivot of the page's own wiring + drug rows — every cell is the book's own; the map view is KYP.
kypExtensions.rationale: The book prints the wiring labels and the drug rows; the state directions beyond the printed mechanisms, the sacral levels, Onuf nucleus, and the retention/incontinence sorting frames are KYP extensions, flagged wherever they appear.
kypExtensions.location: blocks[2] the key map + mechanisms + the visual's wiring annotations

kypExtensions.summary: The four-code memory layer. Code 1 is the SOURCE'S OWN printed mnemonic, carried verbatim and attributed (not a KYP design): BABY ONE MORE TIME — 'Baby one more time.' printed in the margin of book 236 with the red first letters B·o·m·t = Bethanechol · Oxybutynin · Mirabegron · Tamsulosin, the four drug rows in table order (the E38/PH9 attribution precedent — the code itself is First Aid's, so it sits in the note as an attributed quotation). Codes 2–4 are KYP-original designs built on the section's own printed elements: SYMPATHETIC HOLDS, PARASYMPATHETIC FLOWS (the book's own two margin arrows compressed — sympathetic → retention, parasympathetic → voiding); M₃ SQUEEZES, β₃ STRETCHES, α₁ GUARDS THE GATE, NICOTINIC IS YOURS (the four receptor plates with their directions — the M₃-contraction and the M₃/β₃-relaxation directions are the book's own table rows, the α₁-guard and the nicotinic-voluntary readings are KYP); S2,3,4 KEEPS THE URINE OFF THE FLOOR (the classic sacral-level code for the pelvic/pudendal nerves — outside First Aid, flagged as a classic KYP anchor). The layering (which code for which stem, and the attribution discipline) is KYP's design.
kypExtensions.rationale: The KYP memory layer is an original design; where a code quotes the book's own printed mnemonic ('Baby one more time.') it is carried verbatim and attributed inside the code's meaning — the code itself is not a KYP creation. The remaining three codes are KYP-original designs built on the section's own printed elements (the arrows, the receptor plates, the nerve lanes).

notes: Census (pdfimages + text layer + VLM): the Micturition control section occupies the UPPER portion of pdf 258 (book 236), ending at the drug table's last row — the LOWER portion opens the SEPARATE pending 'Tissue distribution of adrenergic receptors' section (same-page boundary pinned), and pdf 259 opens the SEPARATE pending 'G-protein–linked second messengers' section (259-side boundary pinned). The section's printed content: (1) the MIC turition WIRING DIAGRAM — a full-color medical illustration (3 sep rasters: the bladder-base/trigone mask 426x336, the bladder+urethra body 383x518, a curved wall segment 458x277 — COPYRIGHTED tissue artwork, NEVER reproduced) with vectorized typeset labels: three input nerves (Pelvic = parasympathetic → detrusor M₃; Hypogastric = sympathetic → detrusor β₃ AND internal sphincter α₁; Pudendal = somatic → external sphincter Nicotinic), three structures (Detrusor muscle, Internal urethral sphincter, External urethral sphincter), and four receptor plates (M₃ ①, β₃ ②, α₁ ③, Nicotinic) — the numbered circles key the receptors to the numbered drug-table rows (① = the two M₃ rows, ② = β₃, ③ = α₁); (2) the margin note — the pontine center sentence + the two autonomic arrows + the drug-bridge sentence (all carried verbatim in the note's first table block); (3) the printed mnemonic 'Baby one more time.' (red initials B·o·m·t = Bethanechol · Oxybutynin · Mirabegron · Tamsulosin — the source's own, carried verbatim and attributed); (4) the four-row DRUGS/MECHANISM/APPLICATIONS table (carried verbatim; the text layer splits the receptor subscripts onto their own lines — the ₃/₃/₃/₁ of M₃/M₃/β₃/α₁ — documented, composed inline in the note's table). KYP extensions flagged wherever they appear: the storage-state vs voiding-state naming, the α₁-contraction direction (read off the α1-antagonist row), the pudendal voluntary-hold reading, the S2–S4 sacral levels + Onuf nucleus, and the retention/incontinence sorting frames. The registry visual (MicturitionControlMap) conveys the copyrighted diagram as ONE original KYP schematic (the bladder/urethra glyph column, the three nerve lanes, the four receptor plates, the two state panels, the verbatim margin-note strip, the four-row drug strip, the code strip) — nothing reproduced; the drug table is carried verbatim as the note's table block. No copyrighted photographs reproduced; nothing reproduced. The clinical anchors extending past the page (postoperative retention, anticholinergic burden in the elderly, neurogenic bladder after spinal cord injury, autonomic dysreflexia, diabetic cystopathy) are flagged as KYP clinical anchors wherever they appear.
